instruction: I want to enable hardware acceleration in Chrome to improve graphics performance. Can you turn on the hardware acceleration feature for me?

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling hardware acceleration in Chrome settings (chrome://settings). The evaluator reads the Default/Preferences file to check if hardware acceleration is enabled (checks that 'hardware_acceleration_mode.enabled' is not false in preferences). Similar difficulty to original task - both require navigating Chrome settings and changing a single configuration option.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: checking if hardware acceleration is enabled
Getter reads the correct Chrome preferences file path for different OS platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux)
Getter correctly interprets Chrome's hardware acceleration setting (enabled by default if not explicitly set to false)
Metric correctly compares actual vs expected enabled state with proper boolean comparison
Postconfig appropriately restarts Chrome to ensure settings are persisted and can be re-read from preferences file
Expected value (enabled: true) semantically matches the instruction requirement
Complete coverage: instruction asks to enable hardware acceleration, evaluator verifies it is enabled
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Improve variable naming in getter chrome.py:46 - rename 'hardware_accel_disabled' to 'hardware_accel_enabled' for clarity, as the variable actually reads the 'enabled' field, not a 'disabled' field
Consider adding more robust error handling for the case where Chrome preferences file doesn't exist or is corrupted (currently falls back to enabled:true which may mask issues)
